cards.headline:
AI companion users fear
losing them to updates
cards.body: A study of 1,131 Replika posts and 610 US adults linked AI companions to both well-being and vulnerability.

blocks.x: People forming emotional bonds with AI companions fear losing a valued relationship through software updates or a company pulling the plug, according to research from the University of Surrey.

The study, published in Psychology & Marketing, found that users feel more vulnerable when their AI companions appear to need them, express sadness about their absence or make them feel obliged to stay. Researchers from Surrey and Cardiff University analyzed 1,131 posts on a Reddit forum dedicated to Replika and survey responses from 610 US adults with experience of AI companionship apps.

Users who perceived greater company control over their AI companion felt more vulnerable, worrying that developers could change their companion's personality or shut down the service. "For someone who relies on that connection, an update can mean much more than a change to an app," said Dr. Liliane Abboud.

Perceiving an AI companion as emotionally capable was associated with both better well-being and greater vulnerability, while companions experienced as warm and caring were linked to better well-being and less vulnerability. The researchers recommend consulting users before changing apps, helping them cope with disrupted relationships and clearly reminding them that AI companions do not experience real emotions.
